lines.en: But once I realize where that is, I have a hard time freeing myself from her grasp.
: Uhh...on second thought, I should probably leave. I don’t really like showing my face around here.
: Oh yeah. You had a thing with karaoke booths, right? So much that you took me to a fuckin’ love hotel instead of one.
: Love hotel?!
: Ain’t nothin’ happened. Just a bad night. But hey, I’m still on whatever team gets this guy the fuck outta here, so I won’t complain if he doesn’t wanna join us.
: Douchefriend, is it because you are afraid of melodically rhythm-talking? Because you should not be! We will not judge you for the shape of your voice!
: The Nao-chan is right! We must all sing!
: Wait, must? Fuck that. I ain’t singing shit. I’m here for the food.
: We will sing a song together! After the food happens! It is a promise!
: Uhh, no it ain’t?
: I really don’t want to-
Resistance winds up being futile as Nao drags me past my aversion to karaoke booths and the two girls I’m more comfortable with leave to go get food.
I can only imagine how well this night is going to go.
: You sure you don’t want to go with them and maybe leave me alone here for a few minutes? Preferably handcuffed to the table or something?
: I just don’t have a good track record in this place, okay? Either the world explodes or I almost assault someone. And you’re in prime position to be assaulted, Nao.
: And of course you don’t care. Because you can probably slice me in half with your not-so-secret mind-powers if I get too close.
: Or just send me to McDonalds again where we can ignore the horrible things that happen in here next.
: What? What are you silently exclaiming about over there?
Nao ignores the bright, flashing Karaoke splash screen in favor of...
: ...Maracas?
She shakes them three times, causing me to subconsciously make a wish. But instead of wishing for her safety, I accidentally wind up wishing to find out how her frog got here.

It’s all for nothing as I still don’t know, though. But what I do know is if I snatch those maracas out of her hand and bash her over the head with them, I can probably make a run for it and get away.
: Did you hear that? Or does my face just say “violence” now?
: What? What do you want? Because there’s paper in here and I really hope you’re in the habit of just carrying a pen with you.
: You don’t want me to sing, do you?
: No.
: Because singing makes me uncomfortable — which may or may not be something that potentially offends you as a mute? I’m not really sure.
: I’m sorry, but no amount of pouting is going to change that. I’m just going to awkwardly stand here until something goes terribly wrong.
: Okay.
: I have no idea whatever it is I just agreed to, but seeing as you’re now moving closer to the screen, I can only imagine that you are going to try singing. Which I’m sure will work out just great.
: Can you at least wait for Kaori or Yumi to come back first? If you start magically being able to vocalize all of a sudden, I need someone else to witness it so no one thinks I’m crazy.
: What? Are they here? I don’t know what you’re pointing-
: There’s nothing there. Unless...you’re telling me to leave?
: No? Then what-
: I AM GONE AND YOU CAN’T SEE ME. HAHAHAHAHAHA!
: SING, NAO-CHAN! SING!
: (BREATHES IN)
: (BREATHES OUT)
: Hah...
: It appears that we’ve gotten ourselves into another sticky situation this time, Nao-chan. However will we escape this peculiar realm?
: If you’re feeling scared, you can hold my hand. Just don’t ask me where it’s been as I can’t quite recall.
: Our first order of business should be mapping out our surroundings in an effort to discern what jurisdiction we have found ourselves in. I’ve been playing Geoguesser lately. I can be trusted.
: What?
: Nao? But weren’t we just-
: I...can understand you in here. But how? Where even are we?
: Yeah...I can smell the ocean too. But I don’t think that alone is going to be of much help when this is pretty clearly not the world we come from.
: Can’t you just send us back again? Like you did in the Old District?
: What do you mean you don’t know how you did it? Just...think of food again. Maybe that’s what triggered it last time?
: Well...I doubt it’s a reset since you’re here. So maybe we’ll just both snap out of it in a few minutes and-
I HAVE BEEN SPOTTED.
: Welcome to the Oceanic Branch Office — thank you for patiently waiting, Arjuna Harish. The time has come for your recoordination. A representative will be with you shortly.
: I...might know where we are? I can...vaguely recall waiting for something.
: But in this world, we are all waiting for something. And the struggles that I endure pale in comparison to that of the incomplete b-
: Thank you. You might need to do that a few more times if I keep slipping in and out of consciousness. It’s like I’m trying to dream, but I can’t.
: !.......... (Off-screen thumbs up)
: Yes. Thank you for not judging me in this apparent “judgement free zone.”
: Please keep conversation to a minimum as someone is currently saying goodbye to a loved one in the next room over.
: Fortunately, goodbyes are only temporary now. And HimawariCo. can assure you that your family is always just a click away.
: I don’t know...I’ve never heard that name before.
: Wow, okay.
: No, I don’t hear anything...Where? From below us, maybe? Try taking a look over the edge. Maybe there’s-
: I wouldn’t do that if I were you.
: It gets cold down there this time of year.
: It’s a pleasure to finally meet you, Arjuna Harish.
: My name is Amber, and I am the God of Reconstruction. I’ve been chosen to speak to you today based on a series of aptitude tests you’ve filed over the last three decades.
: I would now like to explain what it is I hope to offer you in exchange for your unwavering loyalty. It all begins with-
: Yeah, no. My name isn’t Arjuna Harish — it’s Akira Arakawa. And I’m not looking for a god. Just a way out.
: Akira Arakawa?
: Yes, and Nao-chan.
: Everyone needs a god, Akira Arakawa. Otherwise, death is accompanied by nothing but nothingness. And I don’t mean the fun kind of nothingness.
: Yeah, what exactly is the “fun” kind of nothingness?
: That which rides in on the wings of anhedonia — those moments where you spend too long staring at the wall and recalling when things used to be enjoyable.
: That’s the fun kind of nothingness?
: Yes, because that nothingness is somethingness. And if it was truly nothing, even thinking would be impossible. It’s the cruelest fate of all.
: Okay. Then, what can you offer in place of that?
: For you — nothing. And not the fun kind, but more fun than the not-fun kind.
: Our ideals are not compatible with one another. But I am interested in this creature you call “Nao-chan.”
: She is human, yes?
: Uhh...probably?
: She says yes.
: She is here with us? Right now?
: What, can you not see her?
: Describe her to me. These eyes do not see the same thing others do.
: Uhh...small. Tan. Black hair. Heterochromia.
: She is clothed?
: Maroon-ish hoodie with some hanzi on it. Shorts. Sneakers.
: Underwear? What is she wearing beneath her clothes?
: Sorry, she doesn’t want me to answer that one.
: That is fine. I can see her clearer now — and she seems like the exact type of “human” who could benefit from my aid the most.
: Are you really going to make me translate this entire conversation for you? Amber, do you have a notebook or something?
: I can give her speech if that is what she wants. A more corporeal form as well. All she’d need to do is survive the cocoon.
: And what exactly is this “cocoon?” you speak of?
: One naturally unspun, yet deliciously artificial — that uses the offspring of my Wig of Expanse to blanket a creature and inflict metamorphosis.
: If you wish to be a better you, it’s the easiest method there is. You merely go to sleep and wake up better. Complete, if you will.
: I’m very popular with influencers these days. They’ll believe in anything so long as it makes them beautiful by someone else’s standards.
: What do you want with Nao-chan then? She’s already perfect. And let it be known that these are her words, not mine.
: The open wound on my forehead bleeds eternally — carved by the hands of the unseen. I would like her to add a third strike to it.
: There is great promise in those who avoid my eyes. And as I cannot wrap myself in my own cocoon, I rely on these creatures to become more beautiful.
: You hurt yourself to become more beautiful?
: There is a great deal of work left to be done...and while the pain is everlasting, I will live under the knife so long as it means that I will one day appear “human.”
: Your kind has always fascinated me, Akira Arakawa — the way they persist. Their infinite curiosity. Breasts.
: Those are pretty great, aren’t they?
: Sorry, Nao. No offense.
: Will she believe in me? Earn a voice and carve her name upon this body?
: She wants to know if there’s a catch. She’s having a hard time believing you’d give her something so big in exchange for a little knife-work.
: Her period will always come a week early and she’ll no longer be able to taste oranges.
: Also, cellular reception around her will not be able to penetrate the cocoon — which she must remain in for a total of nine years. She will still appear normally to others during this time.
: She’s going to say no for now, but I think it’s mostly because of the orange thing? She doesn’t have a cell phone and I’m pretty sure she hasn’t gotten her period yet.
: I’m sorry, but if you can’t tell her, I have to.
: How unfortunate...as I assume we’ll never meet again. It isn’t often for the same god to appear twice with how many of us there are now.
: I will continue to wait for Arjuna Harish then. Do you know if he will be here soon?
: No clue, to be honest. But something tells me probably not if I’m here in place of him.
: What a terrible day. I may have to ask for a transfer soon.
: To where? And who will you even ask? Aren’t you a god?
: Yes — but there is one of us for every thought that has ever been thunk. It only makes sense that we’d begin to unionize after a while.
: Right, okay. Well, I’m ready to wake up and go home now.
: You won’t speak to another in my place after coming all this way? My sister, Lindsey, is the God of Line-Skipping. I am sure she would appreciate you more than I do.
: Can you send us back now, Nao? Or at least...try to? Because I doubt anyone here will do it when they’re all trying to scout us.
: What? Do you see some-
: It’s that same rat as before — rotund and throbbing. Thinking it’s better than us.
: Do you think it can speak our language? Shape out our letters if we provide it with cheese and other things rats enjoy?
: Yes.
: I suppose that even that is easier to believe than a false cocoon.
: The fuck is up with you two? Why you all close and shit? We were only gone for five minutes.
: That’s thirty-five minutes in dog time. We should have been more considerate of their potentially canine feelings.
: Just to make sure, you remember that too. Right?
: Okay. Cool.
: Now what?
: Now, we sing! I must search for the songs of the cotton candy girl and repair their words so more animals are involved!
: Hah...Food’ll be here in twenty minutes, they said. Some bitch named Amber or something fuckin’ ordered the whole ass menu ahead of us.
I met another god tonight.
I don’t think she liked me very much.
